WhenWhoWhat

How forms works

A form builder with public links, and a review pipeline for what comes in. Build sections and questions (short and long text, multiple choice, checkboxes, dropdown, linear scale, date), mark them required, branch from a choice to another section. Every form has a random public link; anyone with it can submit while the form is open — no account, no sign-in. Submissions run through received → in review → accepted / declined, with a rating per reviewer, an assignee and internal notes. Charts under Insights, CSV export for the spreadsheet.

Who sees what

People from your hub directory sign in through the hub. A form belongs to whoever created it; the owner shares it with colleagues as editors (build and review) or viewers (read-only). Employees see their own and shared forms. Hub-assigned app admins can access all forms and settings; when someone leaves, the hub lists their forms and an admin reassigns them.

Respondents

Anonymous by default. A form can ask for a name and e-mail (optional or required, self-declared, shown in the review table). If the form allows it, a respondent can edit their answers later through a private edit link kept on their device. A response deadline and a submission limit close the form on their own; drafts and trashed forms are invisible on their public link.

Notifications

A new submission tells the form's owner and editors through the hub (bell, and Slack if they switched it on): title and link only, the content stays here behind sign-in.

Import

Paste the JSON of a Google Form (Forms API) or a plain text outline — tags like [choice], [scale 1-5], [required]. Got a PDF or a screenshot? The import dialog carries a prompt for your AI assistant that turns it into that outline. You get a report of what was imported before anything is created; imports land as drafts.

Trash and limits

Deleting a form moves it to the owner's trash for 90 days — restorable exactly as it was, public link included — then it is removed for good. Limits: 2 000 forms, 5 000 submissions per form, 50 000 in total, 600 public submissions per five minutes across all forms; CSV export defuses spreadsheet formulas in answers.

Paste the JSON from the official Forms API (forms.get). No code needed: copy the form id from your edit URL (…/d/<id>/edit), open the forms.get reference ↗, use the "Try it" panel with your Google login, execute, copy the JSON here.
One question per line, options as "- option" lines below it. Tags in brackets: [choice] [checkboxes] [dropdown] [short] [paragraph] [date] [scale 1-5] [required]. "# Title" names the form, "## Title" starts a new section. A question with option lines and no tag becomes multiple choice.
